profiles.name: The reassurance seeker
profiles.who: Buying once in years to mark a promotion, birthday or anniversary. Wants the right watch, bought safely.
profiles.moment: Sunday evening, a week after the promotion came through.
profiles.quote: I’ll wear this for twenty years. I just need to know it’s the right one, and that I can send it back if it isn’t.
profiles.job: When I mark a milestone with a watch I’ll keep for decades, I want to be sure it’s the right one and the purchase is safe, so I can enjoy the moment without regret.
profiles.confidence_note: Desk research and site walk only; no customer evidence yet.

profiles.name: The value checker
profiles.who: Knows the reference they want and the going price. Compares dealers, grey market and the brand.
profiles.moment: Lunch break, three tabs open: a forum, a dealer and breitling.com.
profiles.quote: I know what this watch goes for. Tell me why I should pay full price here.
profiles.job: When I’ve settled on a reference, I want the best overall deal from a seller I trust, so I can buy without feeling I overpaid.
profiles.confidence_note: Market check and site walk; buying behaviour assumed.

profiles.name: The deadline giver
profiles.who: Buying for someone special against a date. Needs it to arrive on time, look right and be easy to swap.
profiles.moment: Ten days before a birthday, on the phone in the evening.
profiles.quote: Their birthday is on the 14th. If it doesn’t arrive in time, there’s no point.
profiles.job: When I’m buying a watch for someone special against a date, I want it to arrive on time and be easy to swap, so I can give it with confidence.
profiles.confidence_note: Gift offer and policies seen; how givers buy is assumed.
